symptoms.leaf: Angular, yellow spots on older leaves. Spots enlarge and become circular with light brown centers and dark brown borders. In advanced stages, gray centers drop out causing shot-hole or shredded appearance. Under greenhouse conditions, spots may have light centers, rings of olive green tissue, and yellow borders. Severe infection can lead to defoliation.
symptoms.stem_petiole: Elongated spots, helps differentiate from anthracnose, downy mildew, or angular leaf spot.
symptoms.fruit: Darkened, shriveled fruit if infection occurs early at blossom end.

conditions_favoring_disease.temperature: Warm 25–35°C (77–95°F) promotes development; infection can occur at 21–26°C (70–80°F)
conditions_favoring_disease.other_factors: Fluctuating daily temperatures and presence of infected plant residues or weeds

pathogen_lifecycle.survival: On infected plant residues for at least two years, or on weed hosts
pathogen_lifecycle.infection: Leaves, stems, petioles, roots, flowers, and fruits under favorable conditions

cultural: Implement good sanitation in fields and greenhouses
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
chemical: Preventive fungicide sprays according to label instructions
management.integrated: Combine resistant varieties, sanitation, and fungicide programs to reduce disease incidence

references: Cucurbit crop disease guides and extension publications
Global distribution reports of Corynespora cassiicola
